title: Robust Tree-based Learned Vector Index with Query-aware Repartitioning

problem.claim: Cross-modal approximate vector retrieval must handle query vectors whose distribution differs from that of database vectors.

gap.claim: Existing methods typically focus on either in-distribution or out-of-distribution queries and struggle to handle both within a unified framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: Approximate vector retrieval efficiently retrieves similar items from large datasets and supports applications including information retrieval, recommender systems, and large language models.
Representation learning and multimodal neural models embed diverse data types into a shared vector space for similarity-based retrieval.
Cross-modal retrieval creates a distribution shift in which query vectors can be out-of-distribution relative to database vectors.
The distribution mismatch complicates retrieval and degrades accuracy.
Existing methods do not adequately address both in-distribution and out-of-distribution queries in one unified framework.

source_observation.claim: A retrieval system may need to support both matched-distribution and shifted-distribution queries.

interpretation.claim: Query-distribution awareness is a relevant design consideration for unified approximate vector retrieval.

application.claim: Evaluate retrieval approaches across both in-distribution and cross-modal out-of-distribution query settings.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not establish that this consideration applies beyond the described approximate vector retrieval setting.
